title: Stage skill generation and overrides
responsibility: Generate one packaged skill per canonical stage definition, named `kiln-stage-<stage-id>`, so that stage purpose, decision owner, outputs and exit criteria are never hand-maintained twice; fail a check that writes nothing when a packaged stage skill is stale, missing or orphaned relative to `stages/`; and register the consumer's own override directory after the packaged set so an override with the same identity wins without editing the tool clone.
notes: ⚠️ THE GENERATOR EXISTS TO PREVENT ONE SPECIFIC DRIFT: the agent working confidently to exit criteria the application is not checking. Two hand-maintained descriptions of one pipeline disagree, and the disagreement is invisible from either side. ⚠️ THE NAMING RULE IS A CONTRACT (2026-09-13). Every generated skill is `kiln-stage-<stage-id>`, at `pi-package/skills/kiln-stage-<stage-id>/SKILL.md`, with that name in its frontmatter - for example `kiln-stage-01-intake` and `kiln-stage-09-handoff`. The prefix keeps them from colliding with a consumer's own skills, and the full name is the identity a consumer override must match, so it does not change without a migration. ⚠️ GENERATED AND HANDWRITTEN ARE KEPT APART. The generator owns exactly the `kiln-stage-*` skills and nothing else under `pi-package/skills/`. `kiln-planning` is handwritten, and generation and the check must never adopt it, rewrite it, report it as orphaned, or delete it; a skill directory the generator did not produce is not the generator's to judge. ⚠️ PURPOSE IS PART OF THIS COMPONENT, AND IT IS DEFERRED (F88, 2026-09-13). The responsibility above includes a stage's purpose, and the completed component will generate it. TSK-0046 does not, because no canonical purpose field exists today: `producesProse` describes what a stage produces, and printing it as a purpose would be inference rather than generation. TSK-0071 authors a purpose field in every definition and generates it from there; until then each generated skill states plainly that its purpose is not declared.
